Definition: a scraper, i.e. a carving chisel
BiblicalUsage: maqtsuʻâh is a carving chisel, a scraper, and it occurs once, in Isaiah 44:13. There the carpenter stretches out his rule and marks the wood with a line and fits it with planes, and marks it out with the compass, and makes it after the figure of a man, to remain in the house. The word is the tool that turns a tree into an idol.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe maqtsuʻâh warns me that tools in the wrong hands carve idols, and that the same skill can serve God or make a god.
